note: Values plotted in the eight figures, with the location in each source. 'derived' marks values computed here from reported values; the formula is given.

1-grid-upgrade.status: Illustrative arithmetic. Hypothetical 100 MW contract; assumes the customer is subject to both GS-5 minimums.
1-grid-upgrade.source: Virginia SCC, 2025 Dominion Biennial Review Order Summary (Nov 2025); Energy Tariff Experts for PJM, Retail Large-Load Implementation Report, p. 114 (GS-5 summary)
1-grid-upgrade.excluded: Energy (MWh) charges, rates in $/kW, household bills, facility bills, eligibility and exemptions.

global.source: IEA, Key Questions on Energy and AI, executive summary (April 2026 release)
global.scope: Electricity consumption of all data centres, world
global.verification: Values as stated in the article text. The IEA page returned HTTP 403 to automated fetches; not re-checked against the primary page.

virginia_inset.source: Virginia JLARC, Data Centers in Virginia (Report 598, December 2024), printed p. 36 (PDF p. 54)

events.event: Dominion paused adding new data center loads in Loudoun County for three months as it worked to resolve regional transmission constraints.
Dominion incrementally added new data center loads in Loudoun.
Dominion expected the constraints that limit new load additions would not be fully resolved until 2025.
Dominion letter to customers: future large load additions anywhere in its transmission zone expected to take 12 to 36 months longer than before.

3-water-accounting.status: Flow diagram is schematic; flows are not to scale.

definitions.source: Li et al., arXiv 2304.03271 v5, Section 2.1
definitions.withdrawal: Freshwater taken from a source, temporarily or permanently.
definitions.consumption: Withdrawal minus discharge: water evaporated, transpired, incorporated into products, or otherwise removed.

li_et_al.source: Pengfei Li et al., Making AI Less 'Thirsty', arXiv 2304.03271, v5 (26 March 2025; v1 6 April 2023)
li_et_al.workload: GPT-3 (175B) inference; one medium-length response, about 800 words or fewer of input and 150 to 300 words of output; Microsoft U.S. data-center locations
li_et_al.boundary: Operational water consumption: scope 1 (on-site cooling) plus scope 2 (location-based electricity generation). Scope 3 excluded.
li_et_al.headline: 500 mL for roughly 10 to 50 medium-length responses, depending on when and where deployed (Section 1)
li_et_al.formula: water = e * (WUE_on_site + PUE * EWIF_off_site); 0.004 * (0.550 + 1.170 * 3.142) L = 16.9 mL

google.source: Elsworth et al. (Google), Measuring the Environmental Impact of Delivering AI at Google Scale, arXiv 2508.15734 v1 (21 August 2025)
google.workload: Median Gemini Apps text prompt, Google production serving, measured May 2025
google.boundary: Direct on-site water consumption for cooling (ISO WUE Category 2, 1.15 L/kWh) applied to non-overhead energy. No electricity-generation water term.

water_stress.source: IEA, Powering Artificial Intelligence (October 2026), as stated in the article
water_stress.value: Nearly 40% of identified AI data-centre capacity in areas of high or extremely high baseline water stress (location of capacity, not water use)

4-chatbot-removed.source: Bastani et al., Generative AI without guardrails can harm learning, PNAS 122 (2025), Table 1; read via Europe PMC PMC12232635
4-chatbot-removed.setting: Large high school in Turkey, Fall 2023-24; about fifty 9th-11th grade classes, nearly 1,000 students; four 90-minute sessions; classroom-level randomization; honors classrooms excluded
4-chatbot-removed.outcome: Normalized grade on [0, 1]; intention-to-treat regression with previous GPA and session, grader, grade-level and teacher fixed effects; SEs clustered by classroom

arms.control: Course books and notes, no devices
arms.gpt_base: Laptop with a GPT-4 interface similar to a standard chatbot
arms.gpt_tutor: Laptop with a GPT-4 tutor prompted with teacher hints and the solution; designed not to give the answer

exam_unaided.condition: Closed-book, closed-laptop exam, identical across arms

derived.ci95: coef +/- 1.96 * SE (normal approximation; the paper reports SEs, not intervals)

5-early-career-employment.source: Brynjolfsson, Chandar and Chen, Canaries in the Coal Mine? (revised 12 August 2026), Section on young workers, p. 10-11
5-early-career-employment.data: ADP payroll; balanced panel of firms observed monthly January 2021 to June 2026 (3.5 to 5 million employees per month); full-time workers under 70
5-early-career-employment.exposure: Eloundou et al. (2024) GPT-4 beta exposure quintiles; most exposed = quintiles 4-5, less exposed = quintiles 1-3

values.divergence: 21 percentage points, or 19% relative to growth for the bottom three quintiles

5-early-career-employment.interpretation: Authors: early, descriptive indicators rather than causal estimates.
5-early-career-employment.not_plotted: Monthly path between endpoints (shown only graphically in the paper).

6-robocall-timeline.source: FCC, Steve Kramer Forfeiture Order, FCC 24-104 (adopted 26 Sep 2024, released 30 Sep 2024)

events.event: Kramer asks Voice Broadcasting for a Sunday-night robocall, 'probably 25k' calls
Kramer sends the script; Individual-1 creates the AI voice message with ElevenLabs software; paid $150
9,581 calls initiated by 7:12 p.m., with spoofed caller ID of a New Hampshire political operative
The operative whose number was spoofed complains to the New Hampshire DOJ
FCC Enforcement Bureau cease-and-desist letter to Lingo Telecom; NH DOJ and the state AG task force demand Life Corp. cease and desist
FCC rules that TCPA limits on artificial voices cover AI-generated voices
Notice of Apparent Liability proposing $6,000,000 adopted (released 24 May)
NH Attorney General announces Kramer's indictment
Lingo Telecom consent decree: $1 million civil penalty
Forfeiture Order adopted: $6,000,000 (3,000 verified calls x $2,000)

6-robocall-timeline.effect_on_turnout: Unknown. The order does not estimate one.

7-story-diversity.source: Doshi and Hauser, Science Advances 10 (2024) eadn5290, main text; read via Europe PMC PMC11244532
7-story-diversity.design: 293 writers (Prolific, UK) each wrote one eight-sentence story; 600 evaluators made 3,519 evaluations
7-story-diversity.ratings_units: Evaluator ratings on a 1-9 scale; indices are means of three items each (novelty: novel, original, rare; usefulness: appropriate, feasible, publishable)
7-story-diversity.similarity_units: Cosine similarity x 100 (0-100) between a story's embedding and the average embedding of all other stories in its condition (OpenAI embeddings API)
7-story-diversity.missing: Standard errors and intervals are in supplementary tables S3 and S11, which were not read; not plotted.

8-capability-to-catastrophe.status: Conceptual diagram; no probabilities or quantities.
8-capability-to-catastrophe.source: International AI Safety Report 2026 (February 2026); the article's own list of conditions and safeguards
